study.question: Can an unordered timestamp-packet representation recover useful gap/recurrence information lost by deleting tied timestamps, under identical supplied histories and matched capacity? Does any change depend on associating recurrence with elapsed gaps?
study.hypothesis: Observation: direct_lifted validation AUC0.6304316804, probe complete-events mean118.1152344 versus singleton-events mean101.6816406 (16.4335938 excluded), about13.9% of complete events. Its temporal branch bridges over every removed time tie. Mechanism hypothesis: coalescing equal-age complete events into an unordered packet and assigning unit edge mass between adjacent distinct packets retains time geometry and expected field recurrence without inventing within-tie order. This may improve the gap branch. More detailed representations need not help: behavior_within AUC0.6119129 was below baseline-din0.6133620; chronological_joint0.6214969 below chronological_product0.6218837. Compact calibrated/native heads0.6300827/0.6301357 did not match lifted0.6304317 in one seed; retain lifted for this distinct information contrast rather than claim compaction solved. These are exploratory single-seed observations, not significance or repeated mechanism support.

nearest_work.difference: Exact local parent deletes ALL members of equal-age ties, then counts adjacency on the singleton subsequence. Proposed packet branch retains tied complete events as unordered empirical distributions, unit packet-edge mass, and category/brand coincidence probabilities across adjacent distinct timestamps. All pre-gap branches remain singleton-based as before.
Reuse its margin-preserving deterministic recurrence/gap replacement at pooled scope, now crossed with timestamp unit. This replacement is inherited, not novel.

DIN uses ad-conditioned weighted pooling and unnormalized activation to retain intensity. This proposal changes deterministic timestamp adjacency statistics, with no new learned attention; category/brand embedding means are inherited. Local baseline uses softmax and is field-adapted, not an exact DIN reproduction.

README establishes category/brand/type availability and absent item identity. No DMR architecture adoption or full-paper verification. Proposed group probabilities concern these coarse bucket identities only. Broader priority for packet temporal summaries is unverified; registry searches returned no temporal paper or gap memory matches.

inherited_components: Entire direct_lifted source and pre-gap forward, parameter allocation order and embedding system
Complete-pair eligibility history_mask & category>0 & brand>0; no extra events, item IDs, labels, times or fields
Pooled product AFTER aggregation, fixed gap bins, logarithmic counts and lifted4096-dimensional head
Inherited empirical marginal replacement: keep N per gap and each C,B,product channel total across gaps; fractional masses are not realizable reordered histories
study.proposed_difference: Only gap-head input: singleton support deletes all tied timestamp events and bridges gaps, while packet support groups ALL complete events by exact supplied age (including ties), sorts packets oldest first and connects adjacent DISTINCT packets. One edge has total mass1. C and B equal masses are dot products of normalized category/brand histograms of the two packets (independent uniform event draws, an explicitly chosen summary, not a latent event order). Aggregate each by the existing four gaps, then fourth channel=(pooled C)*(pooled B)/(pooled N). No zero-duration within-packet edges and no multiplicity cross-product weights. When every complete timestamp is unique, packet and singleton counts coincide exactly. If all complete events share one timestamp, both give no edges. Two-factor suite crosses support singleton/packet with observed/marginal recurrence-gap association; identical parameterization and arithmetic schedules except selected input. Production uses sort/run histograms O(BL logL) time and O(BL) temporary storage, not vocabulary-sized or pairwise event tensors. No global novelty claim.
predictions: Packet source diagnostics must conserve total mass =max(unique complete timestamps-1,0), have C/B/product between0 and N per gap, and match an independent quadratic event-pair oracle on <=8 impressions. Singleton anchor must exactly reproduce incumbent counts and same-checkpoint logits.

Packet and singleton inputs must agree on histories with no complete timestamp ties, including padding, missing fields and empty histories. Both must be invariant to input-position reversal, bijective field-identity renaming, target/action changes, and adding masked garbage. Packet values must be invariant to a uniform duplication of events INSIDE each existing packet (summary only; inherited full-model logits need not be).

Primary support contrast: packet_observed vs singleton_observed full-population validation AUC; a positive effect with matched parameter count and measured cost is provisional support for the chosen representation, not proof of event-level order. packet_marginal vs singleton_marginal tests whether support benefit survives removing recurrence/gap association.

Within each support observed-minus-marginal contrasts and their difference distinguish association benefit from packet timing/mass changes. Report AUC and unweighted Logloss even if discordant; do not call separate model AUC differences a formal causal mediation estimate.

Review host slices with supplied counts: history_gt64 dominates population(3026583/3234051), sparse1-16(41805,1444positive) and empty8272(310positive) may move through jointly trained inherited parameters. No tie-specific AUC is available through this API; the512-row diagnostic is not a population prevalence estimate.
falsifiers: Any dense-oracle mismatch above floating tolerance (1e-5 count,1e-6 algebraic invariance), negative/subset violation, no-tie mismatch, dependence on arbitrary order within a tie, or nonfinite output invalidates the implementation and bars performance interpretation.
If packet_observed fails to improve primary AUC versus singleton_observed at matched recipe, this implementation is not supported; do not infer tied-event information universally useless.
If packet and singleton differ on no-tie witness counts, this is not the intended timestamp grouping intervention.

If support gains also occur in marginal cells with no association interaction, reject the stronger explanation that restored recurrence/gap association drove the gain; packet timing and bridged-gap changes remain alternatives.
If an effect disappears across paired seeds or is below variation of fresh singleton anchor, classify as inconclusive. One seed and a512-row probe never establish repeated support.
alternative_explanations: Packet representation changes support, adjacency geometry, total edge count and effective fractional recurrence together. The support contrast tests that bundled representation; it cannot isolate tied content from correcting bridges without a later geometry-only replacement control.
Timestamp ties may reflect quantization or duplicated logging rather than simultaneous interests; normalized packet mass may discard useful intensity or suppress noise.

Nonlinear log counts and differing feature distributions can alter optimization, even with identical parameters and allocation. Pre-gap branches share embeddings and train jointly; they are not frozen checkpoints.

Multiple adaptive rounds and validation reuse create selection optimism; probe diagnostics and slices are exploratory. Future paired seeds and frozen validation suite are required; no holdout feedback exists.
Static publisher snapshots have undocumented as-of times, history is capped128 and missing category/brand events are still excluded; no production point-in-time or raw-log recovery claim.
